summary: This document defines a generic structure for the Switching Capability Specific Information carried in GMPLS Interface Switching Capability Descriptors. It can be used by routing protocols with any particular technology, so each new technology does not need its own layout.

eli5.summary: Rather than inventing a new form for every kind of network, this makes one flexible form that all of them can reuse.

questions: what is generalized scsi in gmpls
what is an iscd in gmpls
subtitle: A reusable type-length-value layout for the technology-specific part of GMPLS routing advertisements.

tldr.problem: Each new GMPLS switching technology needs a format for the Switching Capability Specific Information (SCSI) field in routing advertisements, and inventing a new layout each time is wasteful.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines one generic structure: zero or more SCSI-TLVs, each with a 2-octet Type, a 2-octet Length and a Value, plus rules for processing them and a new IANA registry for type values.
tldr.outcome: New technologies can reference this document instead of defining their own SCSI layout. Existing technology-specific formats are not changed.

today: RFC 8258 is a Proposed Standard from October 2017. The unit metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated by another RFC.

sections.title: Why a Generic SCSI
sections.content:
In Generalized MPLS (GMPLS), routing protocols such as OSPF and IS-IS advertise links using an Interface Switching Capability Descriptor (ISCD), defined in RFC 4202. The ISCD has a field called Switching Capability Specific Information (SCSI), and its layout depends on the technology named in the ISCD's Switching Capability field.

RFC 7138 introduced a sub-TLV structure for its technology-specific SCSI, which allows more flexibility in structure, ordering and extension. RFC 7688 uses the same approach. RFC 8258 generalizes it for future technologies and Switching Capability types.

The reader is expected to know the GMPLS architecture (RFC 3945) and the OSPF and IS-IS extensions in RFC 4203 and RFC 5307.
sections.eli5: Network gear needs to tell its neighbours what it can do. Each kind of gear used to need its own special note format. This makes one note format that all of them can share.

sections.title: The SCSI-TLV Format
sections.content:
The Generalized SCSI is made of zero or more variable-length SCSI-TLV fields. The RFC sets no specific size limits on them, though the routing protocol's ISCD field may impose size and formatting limits. Malformed Link TLVs are treated as described in RFC 3630.

  • Type (2 octets): says what kind of information the Value holds and how it is structured.
  • Length (2 octets): MUST be the size of the Value in octets. It MUST be zero or divisible by 4, so the Value can be omitted or contain padding.
  • Value (variable): formatted according to the Type. It can be omitted for certain types.
sections.eli5: Each item is a little labelled package: a label saying what it is, a number saying how big it is, and then the contents. Packages come in sizes that fit neatly in groups of four.

sections.title: Processing Rules
sections.content:
An ISCD can include a Generalized SCSI only for technologies whose Switching Capability definition references this document. It MUST NOT be used for technologies whose definition does not reference it.

A Generalized SCSI MAY contain a sequence of zero or more SCSI-TLVs. The rules are:

  • Sub-TLV parsing (format) errors MUST be treated as a malformed ISCD.
  • SCSI-TLVs MUST be processed in the order received, and if re-originated, the order MUST be preserved.
  • Unknown SCSI-TLVs MUST be ignored and transparently processed, that is, re-originated when appropriate.
  • Handling of several SCSI-TLVs of the same type may be refined by the definition of that type.
sections.eli5: Read the packages in the order they arrive and pass them along in the same order. If you meet a package you do not understand, do not throw it away. Just hand it on.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC introduces no security issue beyond those in RFC 4203 and RFC 5307. The information in ISCDs is not used for Shortest Path First (SPF) computation or normal routing, so the extensions do not directly affect IP routing.

Tampering with GMPLS Traffic Engineering (TE) Link State Advertisements (LSAs) may still affect the underlying transport network. The RFC suggests protecting the transmission of this information with mechanisms such as those in RFC 2154 and RFC 5304.
sections.eli5: These notes do not steer normal traffic, but someone sneaking in fake notes could still confuse the equipment underneath. So it is wise to lock the notes so only trusted senders can write them.

sections.title: The SCSI-TLV Type Registry
sections.content:
IANA has created the Generalized SCSI (Switching Capability Specific Information) TLV Types registry under the GMPLS Signaling Parameters registry. The Type field is a 16-bit identifier.

Value 0 is Reserved and values 1 to 65535 are Unassigned. New allocation requests must say which Switching Type or types the value is to be used with. The registration policy is Specification Required (RFC 8126).
sections.eli5: There is a public list of label numbers so two groups never pick the same number for different things. Number 0 is kept back and the rest are free to claim.

fields.name: Type
fields.desc: Kind and structure of the information in the Value.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Size of the Value in octets; zero or divisible by 4.
